summary: For 10–11 year-olds: use and evaluate parentheses, brackets and braces in numerical expressions, including nested grouping. Learners discover that grouping symbols OVERRIDE the default order — whatever is inside is computed first, and nested groups are resolved inside-out — through evaluating grouped/nested expressions, inserting brackets to hit a target value, and explaining why placement changes the result. This sets up the full order-of-operations convention.
misconceptions: Ignoring brackets and applying only left-to-right or default order.
Evaluating nested brackets outside-in instead of inside-out.
Mismatching bracket pairs in nested expressions.
Believing brackets never change the answer (not seeing they override order).
Dropping a grouping level when rewriting mid-calculation.

activities.title: Bracket playground: move the brackets, watch the value change
steps: Start with 2 + 3 × 4 and position bracket handles around different parts of the expression.
Compare (2 + 3) × 4 = 20 against 2 + (3 × 4) = 14, reading the result each time.
Given the numbers 2, 3, 4 with + and ×, slide the brackets until the expression equals a target of 20.
State in your own words why where the brackets sit changes the answer.
activities.insight: Brackets are a genuine structural operation that overrides the default order — WHERE they go determines which operation happens first, so they change the result rather than being optional punctuation.

activities.title: Collapse the innermost group: evaluating nested expressions inside-out
steps: Evaluate 3 × (4 + 5) by computing inside the parentheses first: 4 + 5 = 9, then 3 × 9 = 27.
Evaluate the nested expression 2 × [3 + (7 − 1)] by resolving the innermost pair first: (7 − 1) = 6, then [3 + 6] = 9, then 2 × 9 = 18.
After each step, rewrite the whole expression with the collapsed group replaced by its single value before continuing.
Colour-code or circle matching bracket pairs so you never mismatch or skip a level.
activities.insight: Nested grouping is resolved from the innermost pair outward; replacing each completed group with its value keeps the calculation tidy and prevents dropping or mismatching a level.

activities.title: Insert brackets to hit a target and explain why
steps: Take 2 + 3 × 4 (which without brackets equals 14, using the convention that multiplication is done before addition) and insert parentheses to make it equal 20.
Write out the bracketed version, then evaluate it step by step to confirm it reaches the target.
Explain which operation your brackets forced to happen first, and why that changes the answer from 14 to 20.
Try a second target on a fresh set of numbers and justify your placement.
activities.insight: Inserting brackets to reach a required value shows that grouping genuinely reorders a calculation: under the convention that multiplication comes before addition, 2 + 3 × 4 is 14, and only grouping (2 + 3) makes it 20. Note that working strictly left to right also gives 20 here, so the learner must write the brackets and explain them; reaching 20 alone does not show the brackets were understood.

activities.title: Checkable practice and spot-the-error
steps: Fill in the value of {2 × [3 + (7 − 1)]} and show each inside-out step.
Choose which bracket placement makes 2 + 3 × 4 equal 20 from a set of options.
Spot and correct an expression that was evaluated outside-in instead of innermost-first.
activities.insight: Grouped and nested evaluations, and bracket-placement choices, can be checked precisely, including incorrect options that reflect outside-in evaluation and ignored brackets.

checkQuestion: Ask the child to evaluate these, watching the order they compute: 3 × (4 + 5); then a nested one, 2 × [3 + (7 − 1)]; then set a challenge — 'put brackets into 2 + 3 × 4 so that it equals 20'. Watch whether they always compute inside the grouping symbols first and work outward from the innermost.
checkAnswer: 3 × (4 + 5) = 3 × 9 = 27. 2 × [3 + (7 − 1)] = 2 × [3 + 6] = 2 × 9 = 18. And (2 + 3) × 4 = 20. The teacher watches for computing the bracketed part first, resolving the innermost bracket before the outer, and correctly placing brackets to force a different order.
